findings.message: `_max_iter_count` is computed with a dedicated `jq` process then `_convergence_json` is computed with a second `jq` process using the identical `.cycle_iterations … select(.value.status == "max_iterations")` filter; `_max_iter_count > 0` is fully implied by `_convergence_json != "[]"`, so the first spawn and the numeric check are dead weight.

Three separate `jq` subshells are forked on `state_file` (status, count, convergence JSON) where a single `jq` call producing a composite object would suffice; the overhead is bounded to one PR-open per run but the pattern sets a precedent for accumulation.

`_pr_open_render_gate_section` forks three `jq` subshells on the same `gate_path` (verdict, failed list, reason) where a single `jq` call projecting all three fields at once would eliminate two process-spawn round-trips.
